dataset_title: Two-stage polyimide membrane biogas-upgrading pilot: abstract-level observations and modeled normalization
geography: Thessaloniki municipal wastewater treatment plant, Greece
material_scope: Biogas from anaerobic digestion of municipal wastewater sludge; two commercial polyimide hollow-fiber membranes in a two-stage configuration with recycle
data_handling: Only discrete numerical values stated in accessible abstracts are transcribed. No graphs; tables; supplementary files; or raw time series were digitized. Pilot observations and model-normalized counterfactuals are distinguished in the CSV.
license_and_access: The journal article full-text reuse license could not be verified from the accessible record. The thesis repository states that thesis files are copyright-protected and PDF download requires free registration. Public repository metadata availability does not imply a license for thesis content. Only minimal abstract-level facts are transcribed.
transferability: Technical comparator only. Feed is municipal wastewater-sludge biogas, not GreenHub grass-derived biogas; gas contaminants; scale; membrane hardware; pretreatment; and operating conditions differ.
known_discrepancy: The journal abstract reports 67% methane recovery for an N2-absence normalized model case, while the related 2024 doctoral dissertation repository abstract reports 87.8% for a binary-gas normalized case. The abstracts do not establish whether the modeled cases or definitions are identical. Preserve both records separately and do not average; choose; or activate either value without inspecting full methods and supporting data.
limitations: Accessible abstract does not state exact pressure; flow reference conditions; stage cuts; membrane area; run count; uncertainty; or complete mass/composition balances.
The published pilot averages have no reported dispersion in the accessible abstract.
The product nitrogen is attributed to air interference during pretreatment; the methane composition therefore should not be interpreted as the membrane's binary CH4/CO2 separation capability.
The N2-free values are model-normalized; not measured pilot observations.
No GreenHub parameter; runtime default; process result; TEA; LCA; or Pareto calculation consumes these values.
